entry_conditions: Use causal world-frame qpos/qvel (including both finger positions and velocities), TCP/red/blue poses (metres, wxyz quaternions), drawer displacement d and velocity, and goal positions. Pass the most recent two observations if available; duplicate a single observation when there is no earlier history. This model re-infers its own finite-window contact belief and does not consume another policy's hidden state. It covers incoming red descent and release, not merely blue insertion. Measured earliest entries have d about 0.300 m, red/TCP near z=0.211 m and total finger width about 0.03649 m while red is still held. Later entries can have red on the pad, moving/open fingers, empty travel, blue approach, or blue lifting. These are training-support descriptions, not hard guards. At blue height, open and closed observations differ across demonstrations: demo1000:815 has approximately 0.0182 m per finger, whereas demo1001:815 is still about 0.040 m per finger. Source timestep is not an input or a contact-state indicator.
exit_conditions: The learned sequence can progress from red-held to red-released/free, blue-source-contact/closing, blue-held transport, lowered-blue, release/retreat and released-clear. Useful optional terminal observations have red on its outside pad at z about 0.020 m, blue near its drawer placement at z about 0.063 m, d about 0.2973-0.2974 m, each finger about 0.040 m, and TCP near z=0.323 m. Increasing TCP-blue separation while blue remains at its placement location supports decoupling. These are optional continuation/transfer cues, not extra completion requirements. A simultaneous successful observation may already occur with blue held near z=0.067 m, as at demo1000:980 and demo1011:980. Release confidence alone never establishes task success.
overlap_role: Retain all assigned expanded slices unchanged, including their 270-278-action overlap with evacuate_red. The overlap teaches incoming red grasp persistence and descent, finger opening at the red pad, TCP retreat with red remaining on the pad, empty travel, approach to blue, closure while supported and the onset of blue-TCP co-motion during lift. Demo1000 spans overlap [575,845), demo1001 [581,859), and demo1011 [575,846); cited 845/846 boundary observations also lie in this policy's expanded slice. Relative position increments, actual fingers and arm velocity let the same learned diffusion policy take over partway through these transitions without replaying a fixed prefix. Empty travel and held transport are distinguished by observed object motion, not by elapsed time. This support does not include an unseen drop or obstruction.
successor_readiness: Give any successor or terminal monitor the actual latest causal state/history, including d, both objects and goals, TCP pose, fingers and qvel. Private latent semantics need not and should not be transferred. For a released-object continuation, prefer measured open fingers and blue remaining near z=0.063 m while the TCP separates, rather than a single contact-mode label. For immediate task termination, evaluate the exact simultaneous contract: d strictly greater than 0.26 m, red inside its pad with center z in (0.014,0.031) m, and blue fully XY-contained in the cavity centered at [0.19-d,0] with center z in (0.053,0.074) m. Use measured wxyz rotations and 0.02 m block half-size for XY extents. Release, tool clearance, object speed and sustained holding are not required. Geometric completion can precede release readiness; these must not be conflated.
failure_signatures: Potential warning evidence includes blue remaining at its source while TCP rises despite an inferred held mode; retreat while blue still follows the tool when release was intended; release while blue height is outside the required interval; unexpected reverse transitions; loss of the red-pad or drawer-open conditions; or inconsistent object/tool motion. These are monitoring concerns, not implemented rejection thresholds or established recovery triggers. Successful data include finger-velocity asymmetry, for example demo1011:845-846, so asymmetric velocities alone do not diagnose grasp failure. The learned probabilities cannot certify attachment or diagnose a novel contact.
continuation_guidance: Continue this policy through the full incoming release/acquisition/insertion transition when measured observations remain compatible with that motion. If the simultaneous task geometry already succeeds but blue is still held, the caller may stop immediately under the contract or retain this policy for useful optional finger opening, settling and retreat. During continued release, monitor actual decoupling rather than requiring a preset delay. Transfer to another manipulation policy only after it has received actual current observations and can re-infer its own state. The model internally reduces persistence of current-contact conditioning when predicted entropy or contact-change hazard is high; it does not change the external execution prefix. The supported framework still executes eight steps and no switching-confidence or invocation-duration threshold has been validated here.
limitations: Observed support comes from successful demonstrations in the assigned full slices. Co-motion and finger widths provide weak attachment/support labels without force sensing; stationary supported and held poses can remain ambiguous. Only two causal frames are available, and duplicate history is conservatively treated as missing older information. There is no persistent recurrent carry, previous-command input, actual adaptive execution scheduler, IK, physical constraint projection, calibrated uncertainty or demonstrated recovery. The learned auxiliary motion predictor is not a verified simulator. End-state statistics and cited observations are evidence, not closed-loop policy performance.
